qa_pairs.question: How can I access a pre-configured JupyterLab environment on the Nibi cluster using Open OnDemand?
qa_pairs.answer: To access a pre-configured JupyterLab environment on the Nibi cluster, first log into the Nibi Open OnDemand portal (ondemand.sharcnet.ca). From the top menu, click on 'Compute Node' and then select 'Nibi JupyterLab'. This will open a form where you can request a new session. After completing the form with your requirement details, click 'Launch'. Once the status changes to 'Running', click 'Connect to Jupyter' to open JupyterLab in your web browser.

qa_pairs.question: How do I run JupyterLab using my own Python virtual environment on the Nibi cluster via Open OnDemand?
qa_pairs.answer: To run JupyterLab with your own Python virtual environment on the Nibi cluster via Open OnDemand, log into the Nibi Open OnDemand portal (ondemand.sharcnet.ca). From the top menu, click 'Compute Node' and select 'Compute Desktop'. After completing the form with your requirements, click 'Launch'. Once the session is 'Running', click 'Launch Compute Desktop' to connect to the desktop. On the Compute Desktop, right-click in a blank area and select 'Open in Terminal'. In the terminal, you can create or activate your Python virtual environment. If JupyterLab is not installed, use the command `pip install --no-index jupyterlab`. Then, launch JupyterLab with `jupyter-lab --notebook-dir $HOME`.

qa_pairs.question: What are the compilation requirements for using AMD MI300A nodes on the Nibi cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: To properly use AMD MI300A nodes on the Nibi cluster, your code must be compiled with ROCm; code compiled with CUDA will not work. As of May 2026, support for MI300A in the software stack is in early stages, so there are no modules available with ROCm support. Users should install software themselves, building against the ROCm toolkit found in the `/opt/rocm` directory.
